meta_title: Generator Tracker — run hours, fuel and maintenance for every generator
meta_description: Track generator run hours, fuel refills and service intervals. Works offline, no tracking, open source. On Google Play and the App Store.
og_alt: Generator Tracker on Android and iPhone: run hours, fuel and maintenance for every generator
hero_eyebrow: Now on Google Play and the App Store
hero_lead: Start and stop a generator in one tap, see how much fuel is left and never miss an oil change — for one backup unit at home or a whole fleet. Works offline. Syncs only if you want it to.
hero_note: No tracking · Open source · Free editions with removable ads
hero_shot_main_alt: Generator screen on Android: a running session with a live clock, fuel left in the tank, engine hours and the sessions list
hero_shot_second_alt: Home screen on iPhone in the true-black dark theme: a running generator on top with a Stop button, idle generators below with Start
features_lead: The power goes out — start the generator in one tap — keep an eye on it — don't miss the service. Everything else the app works out for you.
f_session_d: Running generators move to the top with a live timer and a big Stop button; idle ones sit below with Start. Stopped by mistake? Undo brings the session back with its original start time.
f_fuel_d: Give a generator its tank size and the app keeps a running estimate — "≈ 2.4 L · ~4.8 h left" — from refills and run time. A refill takes a few taps: to full, same as last time or a stepper.
f_service_d: Oil, filters, spark plugs — set intervals by engine hours, by days or both. Each task shows how much of the interval is used, and overdue work is flagged on the home screen with ▲.
f_analytics_d: Run hours and fuel by month for the last six months, split by generator colour — petrol and diesel are never summed into one bar — plus totals per generator.
f_fleet_d: From a single home backup unit to a rental fleet. Several generators can run at once; a live bar keeps the running ones a tap away on every screen.
f_sync_d: Sign in with email — or Google on Android — to keep a phone and a tablet in step. Edits made offline merge safely once you are back online.
f_theme_d: Warm paper light theme, true-black dark theme for OLED and night outages, plus a guide to the system red filter. English or Ukrainian.
how_title: Three steps, and the generator is on the record
how_lead: No setup wizard, no manual. Everything else the app works out by itself.
step1_d: Name, model and power. One unit or a whole fleet — each gets its own history.
step2_d: Tap Start on the home screen when the power goes out and Stop when it comes back. Fuel used and engine hours are worked out for you.
step3_d: Set intervals in hours or days. The home screen marks what is overdue with ▲, so service happens before a breakdown.
show1_title: Start when it starts. Stop when it stops.
show1_text: A live clock to the second, fuel used and fuel left in the tank, and big square buttons that are easy to hit in the dark during an outage or with gloves on a job site. Forgot to tap? Fix the start time later.
show1_alt: Generator screen on iPhone with a running session clock, fuel used and left, engine hours and the sessions list
show2_title: Service on time, not after a breakdown.
show2_text: Each task tracks engine hours and days since the last service and shows the used part of the interval as a bar with a limit tick. Overdue and due-soon tasks are flagged on the home screen; one tap marks a task as serviced.
show2_alt: Maintenance tasks on iPhone with interval bars: oil change overdue, air filter due soon, spark plug OK
show3_title: See where the hours and the fuel go.
show3_text: Square monthly bars split by generator colour, all-time totals with litres per hour and a per-generator list — filter to one generator or look at all of them.
show3_alt: Analytics on iPhone: run hours and fuel by month as bars split by generator colour, with all-time totals
show4_text: Presets for "to full" and "same as last time", a stepper for anything else and a preview of the level after the refill. A full tank calibrates the estimate, and the app tells you when it was off.
show4_alt: Refill sheet on Android: litre stepper, to-full and same-as-last-time presets, filled-to-full checkbox and the level after the refill

compare_lead: You can write hours down anywhere. The difference is what you can do with them afterwards.

cmp_r5: Fuel left estimate and live timer

platforms_lead: Not a web page in a wrapper. Material 3 on Android, the native iOS design — including Liquid Glass — on iPhone and iPad.
pl_android_d: Material 3 navigation, system dialogs and dark theme. Phones, tablets and foldables. The paid Generator Tracker has no ads and no limits; the free Generator Tracker Lite is on Google Play too.
pl_ios_d: Native navigation bars, SwiftUI forms, SF Symbols and Liquid Glass on iOS 26. Free, with ads and limits you can remove once.
pl_android_alt: Generator list on Android in the light theme
pl_ios_alt: Generator list on iPhone in the light theme
privacy_lead: Generator Tracker stores everything on your device first. An account is optional and used only to sync your own records between your devices.
pv_local_d: Every record is saved on the device; the app is fully usable without an account or a connection.
pv_track_d: No analytics SDKs, no profiling. The free editions show ads you can remove once; the paid Android app has none. Nothing is sold or shared.
pv_open_d: The full source code is on GitHub under the MIT license — anyone can check what the app does.
q1: Are there ads or in-app purchases?
a1: The paid Android app has no ads and no purchases. The iOS app and Generator Tracker Lite on Android are free, with ads and a limit of 3 generators (2 maintenance tasks each); "Remove ads" and "Unlimited" cost $0.99 each, "Everything" $1.49 — one-time purchases, no subscriptions, restored on any device with the same store account.
q2: Does it work without the internet?
a2: Yes. Everything is stored on your device and works offline. If you sign in, changes sync automatically when a connection is available.
a3: Android phones, tablets and foldables on Android 7.0 and newer; iPhone and iPad on iOS and iPadOS 16.4 and newer.
q4: Can I use it for several generators?
a4: Yes — add as many as you need. Each one keeps its own sessions, refills, service plan and statistics.
q5: How do I delete my data?
a5: Data stored only on your phone is removed when you delete it in the app or uninstall the app. To delete your account and everything synced to the cloud, open Settings → Delete Account; if you no longer have the app, email yuri.valigursky@gmail.com. Details are in the privacy policy.
a6: English and Ukrainian. The app follows your device language and can be switched in Settings.
a7: Yes. Generator Tracker is open source under the MIT license — the full code, including this website, is on GitHub.

dl_og_alt: Download Generator Tracker free for iPhone, iPad and Android
dl_lead: A logbook for your generator. Tap Start and Stop, and the app counts run hours, shows how much fuel is left and reminds you about oil, filters and spark plugs. Free on iPhone, iPad and Android. It works offline, and you don't need an account.
dl_req_ios: iPhone and iPad — Generator Tracker, iOS and iPadOS 16.4 or newer
dl_req_android: Android — Generator Tracker Lite, Android 7.0 or newer
dl_note: No account · No subscription · Open source
dl_free_title: What you get in the free version
dl_free_lead: The free version does the whole job. The limits are stated here in full, so nothing surprises you after you install it.
dl_c1_d: One-tap Start and Stop, run hours, fuel left in the tank, refills, maintenance reminders by hours or days, and monthly charts.
dl_c2_d: The free version holds up to 3 generators and 2 maintenance tasks for each one. Records you already have are never hidden or deleted.
dl_c3_d: Ads appear on the Analytics and Settings screens. Never on the home screen, never around Start and Stop, never at launch.
dl_c4_d: “Remove ads” $0.99, “Unlimited” $0.99, or “Everything” $1.49. One-time purchases, no subscription, restored on your other devices.
dl_ed_title: Free or paid: what is the difference?
dl_ed_lead: Both editions track the same things in the same way. The paid Android app simply has no ads, no limits and no purchases.
dl_ed_caption: Free and paid editions of Generator Tracker compared
dl_ed_r5_free: Up to 3 — unlimited after a one-time purchase
dl_paid_title: Rather pay once and never see an ad?
dl_paid_text: On Android there is a paid Generator Tracker with no ads, no limits and no purchases inside. On iPhone and iPad you get the same with the one-time “Everything” purchase in the free app.
dl_how_lead: No sign-up and no setup wizard.
dl_s1_d: App Store on iPhone and iPad, Google Play on Android. Both are free.
dl_s2_d: Give it a name. Add the tank size if you want to see how much fuel is left.
dl_s3_d: Tap Stop when it's off. Run hours and fuel are counted for you, and the oil change reminder follows.
dl_a1: Yes. Generator Tracker for iPhone and iPad and Generator Tracker Lite for Android are free to download and use. They show ads on two screens and hold up to 3 generators with 2 maintenance tasks each. You can remove the ads or the limits with a one-time purchase: $0.99 each, or $1.49 for both.
dl_q2: What is the difference between Generator Tracker Lite and Generator Tracker on Android?
dl_a2: They are the same app. Generator Tracker Lite is free, with ads and limits that you can remove once. Generator Tracker is the paid edition: you pay one time in Google Play and it has no ads, no limits and no in-app purchases.
dl_q3: Do I need an account or an internet connection?
dl_a3: No. Everything is stored on your phone and works offline. An account is optional and only syncs your own records between your devices.
dl_a4: No. There are no subscriptions. Every purchase is paid once and stays with your App Store or Google Play account.
dl_q5: Which phones and tablets does it work on?
dl_a5: iPhone and iPad with iOS or iPadOS 16.4 or newer, and Android phones, tablets and foldables with Android 7.0 or newer.
dl_q6: Who makes the app, and can I trust it?
dl_a6: Generator Tracker is made by Yuri Valigursky, an independent developer from Ukraine, where power cuts made generators part of daily life. The app is open source under the MIT license, so anyone can read the code on GitHub. It has no analytics or tracking of its own; ads ask for consent where the law requires it.
